item.title: [8] Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
item.description:
Last authors: Maxim Dzero, Brian M. Andersen

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretic treatment of time-reversal symmetry breaking and Dirac surface states in SmB6, relevant to STS measurements.

Tags: #SmB6 #Kondo-insulator #surface-states

Abstract: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB$_6$ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time reversal symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB$_6$ we find that the interaction between conduction d-and f-electrons drives a surface phase transition near T$_c$ ~10 K in which the time reversal odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface $\Gamma$ and $X$ Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB6.

item.title: [7] Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states
item.description:
Last authors: Mytraya Gattu, J. K. Jain

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Identifies promising fractional quantum Hall candidates for non-Abelian statistics, a significant topic in topological physics.

Tags: #quantum-Hall #anyons #topological

Abstract: The even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, understood as topological superconductors of composite fermions, are predicted to support elementary quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) obeying non-Abelian braid statistics. Using the microscopic framework of parton theory, we investigate many experimentally observed paired composite-fermion states and find that their elementary QPs and QHs in general bind to form Abelian molecules, thus obscuring non-Abelian braid statistics. An exception is the $\nu=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, where our calculations show free QPs or QHs; we thus identify this state as an especially promising candidate for realizing and studying non-Abelian braid statistics. We also indicate how the study of such bound states can help reveal the topological structure of the state.

item.title: [7] Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
item.description:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Valla Fatemi

Authors: Luojia Zhang, Kushagra Aggarwal, Jay D. Sau, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental realization of nonlocal coupling in graphene junctions, relevant to mesoscopic superconductivity and transport.

Tags: #graphene #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. We reproduce the NDLR response with a network containing the interplay between two distinct forms of nonlocality: nonlocal Josephson coupling, which determines the switching sequence of the superconducting network, and nonlocal normal-state conductance, which redistributes current after different regions switch. Our results highlight the potential of the emergent NDLR for characterizing superconductor--semiconductor hybrid systems and for nonlinear circuits. Further, this Josephson Hall bar geometry provides a platform for exploring the interplay between mesoscopic superconductivity and many-body ground states in graphene-based heterostructures.

item.title: [8] Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
item.description:
Last authors: Xingxing Li, Jinlong Yang

Authors: Qing-Bo Liu, Xin-Yi Chen, Xiangyang Li, Xingxing Li, Jinlong Yang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Material-specific chemical strategy for altermagnetism with direction-dependent 100% spin polarization; highly relevant topic.

Tags: #altermagnetism #DFT #flat-band

Abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel. Then, via first-principles calculations, a screening of 90 two-dimensional ambidentate-ligand based square organometallic lattices leads to the identification of three altermagnetic materials, namely Fe(taz)2Cl2 (taz = 1,2,4- triazine), Co(app)2Cl2, and Fe(app)2Cl2 (app = 1,4-azaphosphinine), all of which possess 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in valence bands, as well as notable piezomagnetic behavior. This study paves the way for achieving direction-dependent fully spin-polarization in altermagnetic materials.

item.title: [8] Room-temperature ferroelectric p-wave magnet
item.description:
Last authors: Xianzhe Chen, Ming Liu

Authors: Kaiwen Shen, Nicoly Hembeck, Warlley H. Campos, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Observation of large nonrelativistic spin splitting in BiFeO3; connects ferroelectricity to altermagnet-like spin physics.

Tags: #BiFeO3 #spintronics #experiment

Abstract: P -wave magnets exhibit odd-parity spin polarization in momentum space while retaining zero net magnetization, offering a promising route toward nonrelativistic spintronics. Previously reported p-wave magnets based on combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry, Tt, have thus far exhibited ordering temperatures below the liquid-nitrogen range. Here, we demonstrate a distinct route to a pristine p-wave magnetism that does not require T t symmetry, and instead is based on incommensurate spin-spiral order. Specifically, the cycloidal magnetic structure of the multiferroic BiFeO3 (BFO) intrinsically realizes p-wave magnetism coexisting with ferroelectric polarization at room temperature. Combining symmetry analysis, density-functional-theory calculations, and circular photogalvanic-effect (CPGE) measurements, we find a large nonrelativistic spin splitting of approximately 100 meV associated with the cycloidal order. The resulting p-wave spin polarization gives rise to a characteristic CPGE response whose sign can be reversibly switched by electrically controlling the cycloid chirality. Our results establish ferroelectric BiFeO3 as a room-temperature platform for electrically switchable p-wave magnetism and provide a route toward voltage-controlled spintronic devices based on parity-breaking magnetic order.

item.title: [9] Symmetry-Enforced Topology and Van Hove Saddle Points in Hexagonal TiAs
item.description:
Last authors: Min Zhang, Zahir Muhammad

Authors: Azizur Rahman, Shashi B Mishra, Sheraz Khan, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strong experimental paper on TiAs topology, Van Hove singularities, and Fermi surface; high interest for electronic structure researchers.

Tags: #TiAs #topological-semimetal #Van-Hove

Abstract: We report the first successful growth of stoichiometric hexagonal TiAs single crystals (space group $P6_3/mmc$) using chemical vapor transport and investigate their vibrational, electronic, topological, and magnetotransport properties. Polarized Raman spectroscopy identifies all four Raman-active phonon modes ($A_{1g} + E_{1g} + 2E_{2g}$), consistent with the hexagonal crystal symmetry. First-principles calculations reveal nontrivial band topology characterized by a symmetry indicator $\mathbb{Z}_4 = 2$ and a strong topological index $\nu_0 = 1$, together with symmetry-protected fourfold band degeneracies at the nonsymmorphic Brillouin-zone boundary. The Fermi surface exhibits an orbital-dependent crossover from quasi-two-dimensional cylindrical sheets to a corrugated three-dimensional structure along $k_z$. A Van Hove saddle point approximately 0.5 eV below the Fermi level along $\Gamma\text{--}K$ is associated with a neck-disrupting Lifshitz transition and enhanced density of states. Magnetotransport measurements reveal a pronounced twofold angular magnetoresistance, consistent with anisotropic Fermi-surface geometry and open cyclotron orbits. Hall measurements indicate uncompensated, hole-dominated transport, accounting for the absence of extreme magnetoresistance and contributing to the field-orientation-dependent Hall response. These results establish hexagonal TiAs as a platform for exploring the interplay of nonsymmorphic band topology, Van Hove singularities, and anisotropic electronic transport in transition-metal monopnictides.

item.title: [7] High-Throughput Discovery of Chiral Carbon-Boron Semimetals with Weyl Topology and Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity
item.description:
Last authors: Jinlong Yang, Wei Hu

Authors: Lizhou Yang, Wenneng Zhao, Ye Yang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Predicts stable chiral materials hosting Weyl points and superconductivity, relevant to search for topological superconductors.

Tags: #topological-semimetal #superconductivity #DFT

Abstract: Chiral crystals provide a natural platform for unconventional topological fermions, while light-element carbon--boron frameworks are promising for phonon-mediated superconductivity owing to strong covalent bonding and high phonon frequencies. Here, we combine Wyckoff-position-based structure generation with high-throughput first-principles calculations to search for C--B crystals in selected hexagonal chiral space groups. Starting from 972 generated $\mathrm{C}_m\mathrm{B}_n$ structures ($m,n=1\text{--}4$), successive filters based on energetic stability, dynamical stability, electronic metallicity, topological band features, and thermal stability identify six stable candidates: $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_8$, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_3$, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_4)_6$, $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_6$, $(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{B}_3)_6$, and $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_6$. These materials host diverse topological semimetal states near the Fermi level, including charge-one, charge-two, and charge-three Weyl points, nodal rings, and nodal-surface states. Notably, $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_8$ exhibits screw-symmetry-protected charge-three Weyl points and strong electron--phonon coupling, yielding a McMillan transition temperature of $31.1\,\mathrm{K}$ for the Coulomb pseudopotential parameter $\mu^* = 0.10$. In addition, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_3$ hosts multiple charge-one Weyl points and pronounced anisotropic multiband superconductivity revealed by fully anisotropic Eliashberg calculations. These results extend the materials scope of topological semimetals with phonon-mediated superconductivity to chemically designed chiral light-element structures.

item.title: [8] Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium (Commun. Phys.)
item.description:
Last authors: Mingxun Deng, Huichao Wang

Authors: Zhifeng Xue, Jiaji Zhao, Yi Ji, et al.

Published as: Commun. Phys. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of chiral anomaly and field-induced phase transitions in Weyl semiconductor Tellurium.

Tags: #experiment #Tellurium #Weyl-semimetal

Abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

item.title: [7] Electron- and hole-doped superconductivity in two-dimensional electride ZrX2 (X = Cl, Br, I)
item.description:
Last authors: Xiao-Le Qiu, Kai Liu

Authors: Tian-Xin Liu, Xin-Yang Li, Zuo-Wei Yin, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT prediction of high-Tc bipolar superconductivity and flat-band physics in 2D electride ZrX2.

Tags: #theory #monolayer #superconductivity

Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) superconducting systems have recently emerged as a frontier in condensed matter physics, driven by their unique physical properties and potential applications. Using first-principles calculations, we show that monolayer ZrX$_2$ (X = Cl, Br, I), which is a family of 2D semiconducting electrides, hosts phonon-mediated superconductivity under both electron and hole dopings. Electron doping in ZrX$_{2}$ can achieve high superconducting transition temperatures at very low concentrations, with ZrBr$_2$ reaching $T_c = 30.0$ K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u., followed by ZrCl$_2$ (22.5 K at 0.05 \textit{e}/f.u.) and ZrI$_2$ (18.1 K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u.), for which the high $T_c$ originates from the flat conduction band minimum, with Van Hove singularities nearby enhancing the density of states. In contrast, hole doping requires higher concentrations (0.2--0.25 \textit{h}/f.u.) to activate superconductivity, yielding $T_c \sim 2$ K, and approaches a magnetic instability at elevated doping levels. By comparing with InSe and LaBr$_2$, we identify the spatial location and orbital character of excess electrons as key factors determining the strength of hole-doped superconductivity and the nature of competing orders. These findings establish monolayer ZrX$_2$ as a platform for bipolar superconductivity in a 2D electride and provide insights into flat-band engineering for high-$T_c$ superconductors.

item.title: [7] Equal-Spin local and nonlocal Andreev reflection in altermagnet/superconductor/altermagnet junction
item.description:
Last authors: Xing Wang, Yu-Xian Li

Authors: Kai-Yi Lyu, Xing Wang, Yu-Xian Li

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of spin-dependent transport and Andreev reflection in altermagnet-superconductor heterojunctions.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #superconductivity

Abstract: We investigated the equal-spin Andreev reflection phenomenon in an altermagnet/super\-conductor/altermagnet (AM/SC/AM) junction, focusing on the roles of the crystal orientation angle and the N\'eel vector. The crystal orientation angle in the AM effectively determines the spin-dependent transport channels for both electrons and holes, leading to orientation-dependent local and crossed Andreev reflection in the AM/SC/AM junction. We studied how and under what conditions this equal-spin Andreev reflection occurs. Rotating the N\'eel vector in the AM substantially increases spin-flip channels for both electrons and holes, giving rise to equal-spin Andreev reflection. item.title: [7] Interplay of disorder and spin liquid physics in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet YbZn2GaO5
item.description:
Last authors: Edwin Kermarrec, Fabrice Bert

Authors: Hafsa Zeroual, Shams Sohel Islam, Toni Shiroka, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Microscopic study of disorder and persistent spin dynamics in a triangular-lattice Dirac QSL candidate.

Tags: #experiment #spin-liquid #NMR

Abstract: YbZn2GaO5 has recently emerged as a structurally ideal triangular-lattice antiferromagnet and a promising candidate for hosting a U(1) Dirac quantum spin-liquid (QSL) ground state. However, signatures of broadened crystal electric field (CEF) excitations have raised questions about potential site disorder and its impact on the intrinsic spin dynamics. In this study, we employ 71Ga nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and muon spin relaxation (muSR) to microscopically probe both the structural and magnetic properties of YbZn2GaO5. Complementary muSR measurements further show that the spin dynamics persist down to 30mK, with no signs of spin freezing. Together, these results establish that YbZn2GaO5 presents substantial structural disorder, while the persistence of dynamic spin fluctuations down to the lowest temperatures may indicate the survival of QSL-like excitations despite such disorder.

item.title: [7] Temperature evolution of spin dynamics in extended Kitaev models within an Abrikosov fermion theory beyond mean field
item.description:
Last authors: Daiki Sasamoto, Joji Nasu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of temperature-dependent spin fractionalization and spectral features in realistic Kitaev magnets.

Tags: #theory #Kitaev #spin-liquid

Abstract: The $S=1/2$ Kitaev model provides an exactly solvable setting in which spin fractionalization produces itinerant Majorana fermions coupled to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field. We develop a finite-temperature parton mean-field theory based on the Abrikosov-fermion representation and incorporate the effects of exchange interactions through the random phase approximation to calculate the dynamical spin structure factor. For the pure Kitaev model, the method reproduces a strong, nearly dispersionless peak at a finite low energy together with a broad continuum at higher energies. It also reproduces the momentum dependence of the dynamical spin structure factor and its temperature evolution, including the downward shift of the low-energy spectral weight, in qualitative agreement with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo calculations. Within the present theory, the contraction of the continuum is traced to the temperature-induced reduction of the bond amplitudes, which narrows the parton bands and compresses the two-parton phase space. In the ferromagnetic Kitaev-$\Gamma$ model, the static response develops a finite-momentum softening, indicating an instability toward the period-three magnetic order reported in numerical studies. item.title: [9] Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet -MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
item.description:
Last authors: Oscar Fabelo, Yixi Su

Authors: Feihao Pan, Yishui Zhou, Sabreen Hammouda, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental demonstration of field-induced domain control in the prototypical altermagnet alpha-MnTe.

Tags: #experiment #altermagnetism #neutron-diffraction

Abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, which makes them promising for future spintronic and magnonic applications, but their macroscopic responses can be strongly reduced by domain averaging. In hexagonal $\alpha$-MnTe, three symmetry-related in-plane N\'eel-vector orientations and their time-reversal counterparts form six magnetic domain states, complicating both magnetic structure determination and measurements of the chiral magnon response. Using single-crystal neutron diffraction, we show that an in-plane field applied along the $[-1,1,0]$ direction produces a common magnetic domain orientation that saturates near $\mu_0H=2$ T. A constrained refinement of 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections collected at 2 K and 2 T yields $\mathbf{M}\parallel[1,1,0]$, an ordered moment of $4.62(8)~\mu_\mathrm{B}$ per Mn, and an orientational domain population at $r_A:r_B:r_C=0.97:0.03(5):0$ that is compatible with a nearly complete alignment of orientational domains. Furthermore, an abnormal behaviour in the temperature dependence of the selected reflections is observed in 60-88 K, its microscopic origin is discussed within the context of possible intrinsic piezomagnetic or magnetoelastic effects. Because unpolarized diffraction neither distinguishes domain repopulation from continuous N\'eel-vector rotation nor resolves time-reversal antiphase domains, the field-prepared state is a near-single-orientation state rather than a truly single-domain state. This non-contact domain control provides a practical complement to strain and field-cooling approaches for preparing well-defined magnetic states in bulk $\alpha$-MnTe.

item.title: [7] Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe2/WSe2 with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
item.description:
Last authors: Julian Klein, Alexander W. Holleitner

Authors: Johannes Figueiredo, Kaiyuan Chen, Aubrey Penn, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STEM study using hBN spacers to suppress atomic reconstruction in twisted MoSe2/WSe2 moire superlattices.

Tags: #experiment #twisted-bilayer #STEM

Abstract: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moir\'e superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. item.title: [7] Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi2Se3 single crystalline slabs
item.description:
Last authors: Carmine Ortix, Denys Makarov

Authors: Igor Veremchuk, Pavlo Makushko, Anita Guarino, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Novel nonlinear transport in a prototype topological insulator relevant to user interests.

Tags: #material #topological-insulator #transport

Abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,\mu$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moir\'e heterostructures.

item.title: [7] Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
item.description:
Last authors: Naman Arora, Adarsh Ganesan

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Twisted bilayer TMDs and heterostructures are key broader interests.

Tags: #material #twisted-bilayer #phonons

Abstract: Phononic frequency combs are equidistant spectral ladders generated when a driven vibrational mode transfers energy to an autoparametrically excited subharmonic mode through anharmonic intermode coupling. In previous studies, the coupling strength governing this energy transfer has typically been treated as a free parameter, extracted from a fabricated device, or adopted from an earlier calculation for a specific mode pair. As a result, whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb, and the drive strength required to generate it, has not been predictable a priori. Here we obtain the complete parameter set from density functional theory. Twisted bilayers of \MoSSe{} and \MoSMoSe{} at the commensurate angle $21.787^{\circ}$ adopt space group $P3$ in a 42-atom \rootseven{} moir\'e supercell. The second-order force constants provide the mode frequencies; the third-order constants provide the linewidths through the Boltzmann transport equation and hence the quality factors; and the same third-order tensor projected onto the phonon eigenvectors of a chosen mode pair provides the anharmonic couplings $\kt$ and $\kss$. Both bilayers constitute a mode pair within $0.8\%$ of the $2\!:\!1$ resonance with $\omega_1/\omega_2 = 1.9923$ in \MoSSe{} and $1.9943$ in \MoSMoSe{}. By integrating the resulting two-mode equations, both modes generate combs through a discontinuous transition: at $701\,\fth$ in \MoSSe{} the envelope variance rises from $2.1\times10^{3}$ to $1.37\times10^{4}$ and the tooth count of mode 1 from 7 to 16 within a single $5\,\fth$ increment, identifying the onset as subcritical. The spectral entropy peaks \emph{before} this jump, at $341\,\fth$. The two compounds carry comparable coupling, differing by a factor of $1.2$. However, the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality-factors of signal modes: $Q_2 = 672$ for \MoSSe{} and $Q_2 = 3844$ for \MoSMoSe{}.

item.title: [8] Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
item.description:
Last authors: Wangqian Miao, Chunli Huang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects graphene, STM imaging, and unconventional pairing mechanisms.

Tags: #material #graphene #superconductivity #STM

Abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy has directly imaged electronic crystals in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, and magnetotransport measurements suggest that superconductivity and charge-density-wave order emerge from a common spin-valley-polarized ferromagnetic metal at nearby carrier densities. Motivated by these observations, we ask whether collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate pairing in this setting. We address this question by studying the Cooper problem for two electrons in the first conduction band of the Wigner crystal. Unlike conventional phonon-mediated pairing, the collective mode (boson) energies and single-particle (fermion) dispersion are comparable scales controlled by the electron density, leaving no small parameter for an adiabatic expansion. Moreover, because the magnetic Wigner crystal is not time-reversal invariant, the usual Cooper logarithmic divergence in the pairing susceptibility is absent, so the attraction must exceed a finite threshold for pairing to occur. These unusual features motivate a numerical experiment to see whether the crystal's own vibrations can bind electrons. We obtain the crystalline ground state and its collective mode spectrum within Hartree--Fock and time-dependent Hartree--Fock approximation, and derive the electron--phonon Hamiltonian using the quasiboson approximation. Solving the resulting two-electron problem, we find that phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, with chiral $p$-wave pairing as the leading instability. Within these approximations, we show that collective modes of a Wigner crystal can indeed favor chiral pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry. Our results provide an encouraging starting point for developing a full many-body theory to study electronic crystallization and superconductivity.

We map its quantum phase diagram using density matrix renormalization group calculations and probe corresponding signatures experimentally in arrays containing more than 110 atoms. Experiments on finite open arrays reveal signatures consistent with these regimes across three boundary-pinning conditions, with the resulting response maps agreeing qualitatively with the calculated phase diagram. Our results establish programmable Rydberg-atom arrays as tools for exploring frustrated, material-motivated Hamiltonians and motivate searches for new, quantum-driven magnetization plateaus and quantum-dimer behavior in ErB$_4$ under a transverse field or in strain-tuned TmB$_4$.

item.description:
Last authors: Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie

Authors: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, et al.

Why: Theory of exciton magnetism in van der Waals materials; relevant to electronic structure and magnetism.

Abstract: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. item.title: [7] Deterministic domain selection of antiferromagnets via magnetic fields
item.description:
Last authors: Sophie F. Weber, Veronika Sunko

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetic domain control in MnBi2Te4; highly relevant topological magnetic material.

Tags: #topological #antiferromagnet #vanderWaals

Abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) hold promise for applications in digital logic. However, switching AFM domains is challenging, as magnetic fields do not couple to the bulk antiferromagnetic order parameter. Here we show that magnetic-field-driven switching of AFM domains can in many cases be enabled by a generic reduction of magnetic exchange at surfaces. We use statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo simulations to demonstrate that an inequivalence in magnetic exchange between top and bottom surface moments, combined with the enhanced magnetic susceptibility of surface spins, can enable deterministic selection of antiferromagnetic domains depending on the magnetic-field ramping direction. We further show that this mechanism provides a natural interpretation for experimental observations of hysteresis in magneto-optical response of the van der Waals AFM $\mathrm{MnBi_2Te_4}$. Our findings highlight the critical role of surface spins in responses of antiferromagnets to magnetic fields. Furthermore, our results suggest that antiferromagnetic domain selection via purely magnetic means may be a more common and experimentally accessible phenomenon than previously assumed.

item.title: [8] Anomalous Edge Contrast in Magnetic Force Imaging of 2D Topological Insulators
item.description:
Last authors: Vojislav Krstic, D. L. Carroll

Authors: Timothy W. Carlson, Motahhare Mirhosseini, Allison Swyt, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of topological insulator edge states using magnetic force imaging.

Tags: #topological #STM #insulator

Abstract: Magnetic force imaging (MFM) of 2D topological insulators, such as crystalline plates of Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3, reveals anomalously large contrast around the plate edges even under ambient imaging conditions. And while there are several known contrast mechanisms in MFM, these cannot easily explain the magnitude of contrast observe for such systems. In this work we use multi-parameter magnetic force phase imaging together with a simple analytical model to suggest that the observed magnetic edge-features can be associated with two sources: a pseudo-Faraday effect in the conductive edge channels of the topological system and magnetic scattering in those channels caused by the proximal, localized field of the tip. These results suggest novel MFM contrast mechanisms unique to topological systems and point to the utility of multi-parameter MFM techniques in studies of topological-material-based circuit elements.

item.title: [7] Finite-momentum superconductivity with singlet-triplet mixing in an altermagnetic metal: A pairing instability analysis
item.description:
Last authors: Xia-Ji Liu, Yoji Ohashi

Authors: Hui Hu, Zhao Liu, Jia Wang, Xia-Ji Liu, Yoji Ohashi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of superconductivity in altermagnets; direct relevance to altermagnetism/topological magnetic materials.

Tags: #altermagnet #superconduct #theory

Abstract: We analyze the pairing instability of an altermagnetic metal on a square lattice driven by an attractive nearest-neighbor interaction. This interaction enables multiple pairing channels, including even-parity extended $s$-wave and $d$-wave states, as well as two odd-parity $p$-wave channels. We verify that altermagnetic spin-splitting in the single-particle dispersion gives rise to finite-momentum pairing between electrons with unlike spins, in agreement with earlier predictions. Quite unexpectedly, this pairing typically emerges across multiple channels with mixed parity. Consequently, the resulting finite-momentum Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconducting phase is expected to exhibit a multi-component order parameter featuring singlet-triplet mixing. We examine several forms of altermagnetism, specifically $d_{xy}$-wave and $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$-wave altermagnetic couplings, and present the corresponding phase diagrams. Additionally, we study triplet pairing between electrons with identical spins and find that it always occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum. Although it is unfavorable in the regime of weak altermagnetic coupling and low electron filling, it can dominate the phase diagram when the altermagnetic coupling is sufficiently strong. The influence of on-site attractive interactions on mixed-parity pairing is also explored.

item.title: [9] Engineering superconductivity on the surface of Weyl semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Riccardo Vocaturo, Mattia Trama

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Surface superconductivity in Weyl semimetals; highly relevant to user interest in topological materials.

Tags: #Weyl #superconduct #topological

Abstract: Ten years after the experimental discovery of Weyl semimetals, theoretical and experimental work has pointed to the possibility of realizing surface-only superconductivity at relatively high temperatures in these materials. A consensus is developing that this unusual form of superconductivity is supported by surface electronic states unique to Weyl semimetals, known as Fermi arcs. In this work, we show that the topological protection of these exotic states can be exploited to engineer high critical temperatures. Motivated by reports of van Hove singularities on the surface of PtBi$_2$-the first Weyl semimetal in which surface superconductivity was unequivocally linked to its Fermi arcs-we demonstrate how such singularities can be engineered through the deposition of a suitable additional layer. We find that the critical temperature becomes extremely sensitive to the exact value of the chemical potential, and values as large as 20 times the bulk $T_c$ can be achieved. More generally, our results demonstrate how topological protection can be exploited to manipulate surface electronic states, thereby opening experimentally accessible routes toward engineering high-temperature two-dimensional superconductivity and other exotic phases.

Abstract: Floquet theory describes quantum systems governed by time-periodic Hamiltonians, much as Bloch theory describes spatially periodic solids. Abstract: We formulate the anomalous transverse Thomson effect (ATTE), the long-missing Thomson counterpart of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst effects. Its coefficient is not unique but depends on the electrical boundary condition: $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}$, defined for a spatially uniform imposed current density, and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$, defined for equipotential electrodes. Both are fully determined by the total anomalous Nernst coefficient (ANC) and its temperature dependence, while $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ acquires an additional contribution from the temperature dependence of the longitudinal resistivity. This relation is model independent within local linear response and applies to the total ANC regardless of whether its microscopic origin is intrinsic or extrinsic. Using a massive Dirac model for Fe$_3$Sn$_2$, we show that Berry curvature near the gapped Dirac cones enhances the ANC-related contributions to $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$. In the low-temperature limit, both $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ approach a value of three. We further extract $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ from reported experimental data for CoS\(_2\), Co\(_3\)Sn\(_2\)S\(_2\) and CeCrGe\(_3\); for CeCrGe$_3$ it reaches approximately -20 $\mu V/K$, and we estimate the maximum achievable cold-side heat current density to assess its cooling potential. item.description:
Last authors: Vasile O. Garlea, Matthias D. Frontzek, Andrew D. Christianson, Andrew F. May

Why: Neutron scattering on a quasi-1D magnet exploring frustrated interactions and coexisting magnetic orders.

Tags: #experiment #NdCl3 #neutron-scattering

Abstract: The phenomenon of frustration greatly enriches the accessible physics of quantum magnets. With this in mind we study the magnetism of \NC using a combination of bulk properties measurements and neutron scattering techniques. The low-temperature heat capacity reveals two magnetic transitions at $T_{N1}$ = 270 mK and $T_{N2}$ = 180 mK. However, much of the magnetic entropy is released above $T_{N1}$, manifesting as a broad peak centered at $T^{*} \approx$ 450 mK. A similar broad peak is observed in the magnetic susceptibility, which possesses a clear anisotropy; this data can be well fit using a 1-dimensional XXZ model, yielding an antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange $J_{NN}$ = -0.962(2) K and exchange anisotropy close to the Ising limit. Single crystal elastic neutron scattering reveals highly anisotropic magnetic diffuse scattering above $T_{N1}$, confirming that quasi-one-dimensional, short-range, antiferromagnetic order is the origin of the broad peak in the heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility. Magnetic Bragg peaks characterized by a $\vec{k}$ = ($0$ $0$ $\frac{1}{2}$) propagation vector emerge below $T_{N1}$. Interestingly, the magnetic diffuse scattering persists for $T_{N2} < T < T_{N1}$, indicating a regime of coexisting short and long-range order. The magnetic Bragg peaks exhibit an additional increase in intensity below $T_{N2}$ with no change in $\vec{k}$. Concomitantly, the diffuse scattering disappears indicating the attainment of full long-range order. While the precise nature of the ordered magnetic ground state remains unresolved, the observed magnetic scattering indicates predominate $c$-axis moments with a small $ab$-plane component. We propose that the quasi-one-dimensional behavior and the coexistence of short and long-range order are driven by frustration of exchange interactions with significant anisotropy.

item.description:
Last authors: Yang Zhang, Qianhui Shi

Authors: Jackson Kuklin, Ning Mao, Milan Mandigo-Stoba, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates valley-dependent moire physics and correlated phases in twisted WSe2 systems.

Tags: #experiment #WSe2 #moire

Abstract: Electronic orbital character plays a central role in determining electronic correlations, spin-orbit coupling, dimensionality, and ultimately the quantum phases of condensed-matter systems. Two-dimensional moir'e materials have emerged as highly tunable platforms for exploring correlated phenomena, but the role of orbital degrees of freedom remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify twisted monolayer/bilayer WSe$_2$ as a platform in which displacement-field tuning enables moir'e physics to be realized in both the $K$ and $\Gamma$ valleys. At $ u=1$, the $K$-valley state is a weak insulator, consistent with an antiferromagnetic state near a van Hove singularity in the intermediate-coupling regime, similar to that observed in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$. In contrast, the $\Gamma$-valley state exhibits a pronounced Pomeranchuk effect, consistent with proximity to a Mott transition. At $ u=1/3$, the $K$ valley hosts a robust generalized Wigner crystal, whereas the $\Gamma$-valley state lies near the crystallization boundary and again exhibits a Pomeranchuk effect, with localization enhanced by increasing temperature or magnetic field. Our work highlights the importance of orbital character in defining quantum phases in moir'e systems, and identify the $\Gamma$ valley as a promising platform for exploring correlated phenomena near quantum phase transitions, where competing phases and enhanced fluctuations may give rise to unconventional phases.

item.title: [10] Vestigial chirality from fluctuating loop currents on the kagome lattice
item.description:
Last authors: Xuande Bu, Sheng Meng

Authors: Yin Shi, Xuande Bu, Sheng Meng

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly addresses vestigial loop-current order and TRSB in kagome metals, a primary research focus.

Tags: #theory #kagome #loop-current #TRSB

Abstract: Multicomponent order can melt in stages, leaving a composite order after its primary constituents become short ranged. We study this possibility for commensurate three-$Q$ loop-current order on the kagome lattice. Large-scale cluster and parallel-tempering Monte Carlo simulations reveal direct and two-stage melting regimes in an effective fixed-amplitude sign model. In the latter regime, translation-sector domain walls proliferate before chirality-changing walls, restoring lattice translational symmetry while preserving long-range time-reversal-odd order. The primary $M$-point correlations are short ranged in this intermediate phase. The two-stage regime begins when the lowest-energy chirality-changing wall is only about $12$--$13\%$ more costly than a same-chirality translation wall. Finite-size scaling of a stable amplitude-resolved Ginzburg--Landau theory shows that the phase survives amplitude relaxation. Our results establish a quantitative domain-wall criterion for vestigial loop-current order and a fluctuation route to time-reversal symmetry breaking without long-range loop-current Bragg order. This separation provides a possible thermodynamic framework for time-reversal-odd responses recently reported above the critical temperature for conventional charge-density-wave ordering in kagome metals.

item.title: [7] Uniform-Charge-Density d-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure t-J Model at 1/8 Doping on an Infinite Cylinder
item.description:
Last authors: Guangyu Yu, Zheng Zhu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Numerical study of the t-J model at 1/8 doping, revealing uniform d-wave superconductivity without stripes.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #t-J-model

Abstract: The ground state of the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at $1/8$ hole doping has been the subject of a long-standing controversy, with conflicting numerical reports of stripe order versus superconductivity. Here, we address this debate using the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) method, which optimizes the wave function directly in the thermodynamic limit along the cylinder axis and eliminates the boundary pinning effects that can arise in finite-cylinder calculations. On an infinite cylinder of circumference $L_y = 8$, we find a uniform-charge-density $d$-wave superconducting ground state with quasi-long-range pairing correlations. The dominant pairing occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum, while no sizable finite-momentum pairing component is detected. Twisted-boundary-condition calculations reveal a finite superconducting phase stiffness, with the order-parameter phase winding smoothly to follow the applied flux, providing an independent probe of the robustness of the superconductivity. Moreover, both charge and spin correlations decay rapidly, with no signatures of long-range stripe or magnetic order, in contrast to an $L_y=6$ cylinder at $1/6$ doping where the same method readily identifies stripe order. Our results provide methodologically distinct evidence in the long-standing stripe--superconductivity debate in the pure $t$-$J$ model and reveal uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in a minimal model of doped Mott insulators.

item.title: [7] Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
item.description:
Last authors: Yuqing Jiao, Bert Koopmans

Authors: Pingzhi Li, Gijs W. A. Simons, Tianyu Zhang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental spintronics utilizing anomalous Hall effect readout for on-chip magnetization switching.

Tags: #experiment #anomalous-Hall #spintronics

Abstract: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.
